text: A malicious party intercepted our email communications with Reliance Logistics. They altered the attached PDF invoice (INV-2026-9249), replacing the IFSC and beneficiary account with a mule account. Our accounts payable released ₹4,50,000 against invoice INV-2026-9249. The vendor confirmed their email server was breached and they never issued changed banking coordinates.

Our finance desk received an emergency payment memo from Anand Vardhan (VP Finance) requesting confidential settlement of Rs 2.4 crore under reference UTR UTR453301313. The email came from a spoofed address (anand.vardhan@regalhos-corp28.com) bypassing our spam filters. Believing it was an authorized board directive, the disbursement was executed before discovering the executive mailbox had been compromised.

A malicious party intercepted our email communications with Siemens Healthcare. They altered the attached PDF invoice (INV-2026-7004), replacing the IFSC and beneficiary account with a mule account. Our accounts payable released ₹4,50,000 against invoice INV-2026-7004. The vendor confirmed their email server was breached and they never issued changed banking coordinates.

We were negotiating a commercial contract with Blue Dart Express. A threat actor inserted themselves into the email chain using a lookalike domain (sterling-corp55.com), mimicking our account manager. They provided alternate bank details claiming year-end reconciliation requirements, leading our finance team to wire Rs 5.4 lakh to the fraudulent account.

An unauthorized party gained access to our corporate HR email thread at Heritage Textiles Ltd. Posing as several senior executives, they submitted requests to change monthly salary direct deposit accounts to prepaid debit cards. Several salary credits totaling ₹28,00,000 were diverted before the fraud was detected during payroll reconciliation.

I am an accounts officer at Brahmaputra Steel Industries. Yesterday our team received an urgent email purportedly from our Director of Operations, Meenakshi Sundaram, directing immediate wire transfer of Rs 15,000 to a new account at Kotak Mahindra Bank for an off-market acquisition. The sender address looked identical except for a single letter domain typo (brahmapu-corp52.com). We transferred the funds and later realized the real executive was on a flight.

We are reporting an international wire fraud against Deccan Minerals Corp. An attacker sent a forged message impersonating Rohan Kulkarni, instructing our treasury to wire ₹19,800 for urgent customs clearance and machinery import. The attacker created strict urgency stating penalties would occur if delayed. The wire was processed via SWIFT before the fraud was uncovered.

Our procurement department received an official-looking invoice and updated bank mandate form from our primary supplier, Tata Steel BSL. The email claimed their standard account at Punjab National Bank was undergoing statutory audit and requested all future remittances of Rs 35 lakh be credited to a new beneficiary account. After releasing payment, the genuine vendor called asking why their invoice was overdue.

Impersonation of CFO Sunita Deshmukh: A spear-phishing email instructed our accounts department to split payments of ₹2,80,000 into two installments to bypass daily single-transaction limits. Both transfers were completed to separate mule accounts under forged proforma invoices.
